description:
FOUND s492c (Opus, 2026-09-21) after #2007 made tempdir/tempfile work.

    use File::Temp;
    my $tmp = File::Temp->new(SUFFIX => ".dat");
    print $tmp "data"; close $tmp; print -s "$tmp", "\n";

    perl: 4        PCL: dies in (SETF P-CAST-$) --
          "Cannot dereference non-reference: #<fd-stream for "/tmp/...">"

Core File::Temp's object is a blessed GLOB REF carrying a hash in its glob
slot (`${*$fh}{ISUNLINKED} = ...`), the same representation core IO::Handle
uses -- and PCL's handle is an fd-stream, not a glob ref, which is exactly why
`lib/IO/Handle.pm` carries a rewritten `binmode` ("core dereferences ($$fh)
... A PCL handle is not one").

So this is one representation question with several consumers, not a
File::Temp bug.  Two shapes: make `*$fh` on a PCL handle yield a per-handle
glob whose HASH slot is real (the general fix, and it would also let core
IO::Handle run unpatched), or add File::Temp to the shimmed set.  The first is
the right layer.

`tempfile`, `tempdir`, `File::Temp::tempfile(UNLINK => 1)` and the functional
interface all WORK since #2007; only the OO constructor is affected.


=== s501b MEASUREMENT + WIP DESIGN (NOT SHIPPED — Fable ruling s502: member 5 OUT of the s501b batch; task stays pending) ===
The brief's stop rule was "measure first, ship only if small".  The WIP (commit 948f9e6a on branch worktree-agent-a8afc5670788453d5, dropped by `git reset --hard HEAD~1`) did not meet it: File::Temp->new still fails, the fast-path cost claim is unverified, and the commit was never gated.  The patch is preserved at ~/pcl-agent-scratch/s502/s501b-m5-2056.patch (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp only, +39/-1; applies on 77212b1f/ca44ac4c).

(a) MEASUREMENT (probe scratch/s501b/p/glob1.pl in that worktree; outputs glob1.perl / glob1.pcl = base 77212b1f / glob1.pcl3 = with the patch).  Cells: perl | base | patch.
  LEXICAL handle (open my $lex):
    ref(\*$fh)          GLOB     | REF (X)                     | GLOB
    "*{$fh}"            *main::… | GLOB(0x1) (X)               | *pcl-anonio::__anonio__1 (X)
    ${*$fh}{k}=1        1        | DIE "pcl::h … not a hash-table" (raw CL, X) | 1
    %{*$fh} keys        k,k2     | same raw DIE (X)            | k,k2
    @{*$fh} push        1        | DIE "Type of arg 1 to push" (X) | 1
    ${*$fh} scalar      sv       | DIE "Cannot dereference non-reference: #<fd-stream>" (X) | sv
    *$fh{IO} class      IO::File | GLOB (X)                    | GLOB (X)
    fileno(*$fh)        fd       | fd                          | fd
    print {*$fh}        printed  | printed                     | printed
    bless $fh,"C"       Clex     | Clex                        | Clex
    after-bless hash    3        | raw DIE (X)                 | 3
  BAREWORD handle and \*STDOUT: base fails ONLY `${*$fh}` scalar slot (DIE "Cannot dereference non-reference: #S(p-typeglob …)") and `*$fh{IO}` class (GLOB vs IO::File); the patch fixes the scalar slot; `*$fh{IO}` stays GLOB.
(b) CENSUS of the idiom (`${*$` / `%{*$`) in core modules PCL loads: IO/Socket.pm 28, File/Temp.pm 6, IO/Socket/INET.pm 3, Archive/Tar.pm 1; IO/Handle.pm is shimmed in lib/ already.

DESIGN AS BUILT (the patch): `*$fh` on a LEXICAL handle yields a per-stream anonymous glob from `%p-stream-glob` (a WEAK-key hash table stream -> p-typeglob in package PCL-ANONIO, name __ANONIO__N) whose HASH/ARRAY slots are real; `${*GLOB}` reads/writes the glob SCALAR slot through `%p-glob-scalar-box` (one box per glob).  Only the `*` deref reaches the table — print/readline do not.

STILL WRONG with the patch:
  1. `*$fh{IO}` returns the glob (class GLOB) for all three handle kinds; perl gives an IO::File object.
  2. `"*{$fh}"` stringifies as *pcl-anonio::__anonio__N; perl gives *main::$fh (the name of the declaring lexical).
  3. File::Temp->new STILL FAILS: probe scratch/s501b/p/ft2.pl (`my $tmp = File::Temp->new(SUFFIX=>".dat"); print ref($tmp)`) prints ref=GLOB after new — the `bless $fh, $class` in File::Temp::new does not stick.  The same steps in isolation DO match perl: scratch/s501b/p/bl1.pl … bl4.pl (open my $fh + ${*$fh}{k}=… + bless + ref) all == perl.  So the loss is somewhere on File::Temp's own path.
NEXT STEP (exact): instrument a COPY of File/Temp.pm (the #2080 method: print ref($fh) after each statement of File::Temp::new — after tempfile(), after `bless $fh, $class`, after `%{*$fh} = %$args`, before return) under PCL to find which statement drops the bless.  Suspects: new() reaching the object through tempfile()'s return (a list-return copy of the handle box that is not the blessed referent), or the `%{*$fh} = %$args` assignment replacing the referent, or UNLINK/DESTROY.
COST CLAIM STILL TO VERIFY before shipping: the print/readline fast path must not reach %p-stream-glob — bench `fhread fhprint textproc` A/B (FLAG > 1 %).
The everyday row modules/File-Temp keeps citing #2056.

=== DONE (s502e, Opus, 2026-10-04) ===
THE OPEN QUESTION ANSWERED (instrumented copy of core File/Temp.pm, scratch/s502e/lib/File/Temp.pm + p/ft2.pl): inside File::Temp::new `ref($fh)` is File::Temp right after `bless $fh, $class` and through `return $fh`, but GLOB in the caller.  p-bless's catch-all arm stored a FILEHANDLE's class on the VARIABLE's box only; `return $fh` / `my $c = $fh` copy the payload (the stream), so the class was lost.  Isolated: `open my $fh; bless $fh, "C"; my $c = $fh; ref($c)` -> perl C, base GLOB (p/bl5.pl; list and hash elements happened to keep it).
SHIPPED (cl/pcl-runtime.lisp): (1) the preserved s501b patch -- `*$fh` on a lexical handle yields ONE anonymous glob per stream (%p-stream-glob, weak) whose HASH/ARRAY/SCALAR slots are real; (2) `*p-handle-stash*` (weak, stream -> class): p-bless records a filehandle payload's class there, %p-target-class and p-get-class read it through the inline helper %p-handle-stash-class (a hash-table-count test first, so an image with no blessed handle pays one fixnum compare); (3) reftype of a blessed handle is GLOB.  Runtime diff +77/-6 (most of it comments).  Normative: ir-spec §7.5a table (two rows).
PROBES: p/ft.pl (= everyday/modules/File-Temp.pl), ft2.pl, bl5.pl, glob1.pl (13 rows of the glob-as-object table incl. blessed/reftype through copies) == perl; base differs on each.
BENCH (fhread fhprint textproc + arith control, BENCH_K=5/7, interleaved tree vs 618db500 extraction, 9 pairs, logs scratch/s502e/bench-{tree,base}-N.log): before the helper fhread was +5..7 % in 3 of 3 pairs; after it fhread pairs read +5.4 / -11 / -6.7 / +6.5 / +2.7 % (median +0.9 %) with the arith control spreading +-10 %; load 0.9-3.0 (above the brief's < 2 most of the time -- the bench itself raises it).  readline never reaches the class arm (read).  Verdict: no cost detectable within the noise; not a clean < 1 % measurement.
COMPANION io/ (44 files, --jobs 1 --quick) identical before/after.  Everyday modules/File-Temp `same` (row edited out).
RESIDUE FILED #2611: `*$fh{IO}` is GLOB not IO::File (also *STDOUT{IO}, pre-existing), `"*{$fh}"` is *pcl-anonio::__anonio__N not *main::$fh, and the anonymous glob's name registration in *p-filehandles* is a strong reference (never collected).
GUARD: Pl/t/transpile-test-10.t rows 78-80 (inverse-verified).
subject: `File::Temp->new` dies "Cannot dereference non-reference: #<fd-stream>" -- core File::Temp`s `${*$fh}{...}` glob-as-object idiom
